page.layout: One column of running text, full width, with the page number and running head at the top. Edge fragments of the neighbouring page run along the left and right sides and are not transcribed. Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: lo majorem se fle&tit, atque ita in ortum longissimo tractu ad Sunium usq; terræ Atticæ promontorium postremum procurrit, solo Isthmo Corinthiaco interveniente, quo velut cervice angustâ Peloponnesus cum reliqua Græcia conjungitur: Ante Isthmum autem angustus terræ tractus velut tænia in mare porrigitur; cui similis tænia alia à Peloponneso occurrit relicto tantum freto perangusto, per quod Ionium mare in sinum Corinthiacum proprié sic dictum se infundit, ubi Rhium & Antirrhium oppida aut castella opposita quondam fuêre, quos hoc ævo Dardanellos, freti fauces obsidentes, vocant. Illyridis oram quam dixi, in austrum à septentrione descendentem, coloniis aliquot Græci infederunt, & partem ejus post Lissum urbem, cujus tractum Taulantii & Elimiotæ tenuerunt, Phi-lippus & Alexander Magnus victoriis suis Macedoniæ adjecerunt. Post eam cœpit Epirus, Pyrrho rege præcipuè ce-lebrata, regnum familiæ Æacidarum, [illegible, ~7 letters] populos complexa, Chaones, Thesprotios[?], Antigonenses[?], Molossos, [illegible, ~6 letters]ures alios. E quibus Chaones conter-[illegible, ~4 letters]ini Macedoniæ, per quos Acrocerau-nii montes porrecti procurrunt in ma-re, quorum urbs præcipua litori proxi-ma

page.notes: The top left shows "2§8", read as 258 with the long s. The running head "DESCRIPTIO" is set in spaced capitals. Several words at the start of the list line "populos" are damaged; the reading of "Thesprotios" and "Antigonenses" is doubtful. The line "E qui" at the left edge is partly obscured. The text ends with the catchword "ma", which begins the next page. Several lines are heavily damaged at the left edge, and their readings are conjectural.
